feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning and a coherent career progression in digital communications. It reads professionally and shows breadth across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia, but it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is easy to follow and supports the “Digital Communications & Strategy Lead” positioning.  
- Strong scope and credibility: Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and enterprise workflow/governance work signal real ownership.  
- Writing is polished and generally error-free, with concise, professional phrasing and good use of action verbs.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more outcomes would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, conversion improvements, cost savings).  
- Reduce overlap across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” repeat similar content; consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (currently learning)” or similar.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of seniority, sector focus, or platform scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add a clearer positioning line tied to recent roles, e.g. public-sector/member association digital leadership, Drupal modernization, and analytics-driven operations.
- Reduce broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) and emphasize outcomes or scale instead.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Specializes in web and CMS modernization, editorial and governance workflows, and digital systems that improve coordination across complex teams. Brings deep experience translating policy and technical subject matter into clear, accessible content and stakeholder-facing campaigns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are also reinforced elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and making the phrasing more parallel will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more specific, resume-standard phrasing: “Multi-channel communications” (not “communication”) and “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Replace vague items like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer language such as “Content operations & workflow systems” or “Digital governance & workflow design.”
- Consider a tighter version: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content operations & systems design • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep competencies distinct from tools; leave platform names and software to Topline Skills/Technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy/advocacy communications” are already strongly covered in the header.
- This section overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; consider shortening or using it only for highest-level themes.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Make it more outcome-led and specific about what changed, launched, or improved.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets and add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates, users supported, workflow time reduced, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search relevance gains, or publishing efficiency improvements.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, creating modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing toolkits that improved launch speed and content reuse across teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search is already featured in Recent Projects; keep one concise mention here and avoid repeating technical detail.
- Governance/analytics/editorial systems language overlaps with the header and NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national membership organization.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievements first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add outcome language where possible: “migrated 10,000+ pages to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers” and quantify reporting or production gains if available.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace broad oversight language with a result, e.g., “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and supporting advocacy and member engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- “Governance/publishing standards/planning systems” may duplicate header and competencies unless tied to a concrete operational outcome.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and operational improvements distinct from the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across digital platforms.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built stronger editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier NACo role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating generic “strategy/content” language.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations” or “Content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed verb forms.
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to recent work, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header summary; “communications” is stronger than “messaging” at this level.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, tighten it around highest-value, recent capabilities and group tools under broader themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, impact-oriented phrases rather than a long software list.
- Prioritize recent strengths tied to current/last roles: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, automation.
- Move lower-priority or older/secondary platforms to Technical + IT if space is tight.
- Suggested version: **Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences • WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT” (Web Platforms & CMS; Coding & Technical Implementation; Automation & Workflow Systems).
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent project content; keep wording concise here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT,” so this version should emphasize strategic application and outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability-led, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure & insight generation • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “KPI design” to “KPI framework design” or “Measurement strategy” to sound more senior.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “decision-ready dashboards” or “performance insights for optimization” to show business use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave tool inventory to the technical section.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; combine into “SEO and digital performance analysis” for concision.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment and delivery scope rather than repeating broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production**
- Tighten content to: **Broadcast-style video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and control-room workflows • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid/virtual event production**
- If accurate, add scale/scope language instead of generic terms: e.g., **multi-camera production**, **broadcast-quality studio operations**, or **end-to-end event delivery**
- Keep phrasing noun-based and parallel; avoid “video production and editing” if editing is not a major differentiator elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the NACo role; don’t also repeat “built first in-house studio” elsewhere in skills language

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since recent experience is heavily Drupal-led, this item should emphasize depth/order and trim lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling strength: **Drupal (expert) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: **CMS platforms: Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content systems), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially used in recent roles; it reads lighter than the enterprise/public-sector platforms.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **CMS platforms** or **Web platforms & CMS** consistently across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid listing the exact same platforms in both places without added context.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so this section should complement that evidence, not repeat it verbatim.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless the CV uses versioning consistently; they add little value for a senior digital leader.
- Consider replacing **jQuery** with a broader phrase like **JavaScript (including legacy jQuery environments)** if you still need to signal maintenance capability without dating the profile.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g. **front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- **API integrations** and technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies and recent consulting bullets.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**.
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: **Built and managed workflow systems using Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery in Jira, Asana, Trello and Basecamp.**
- Prioritize the most relevant tools first; if space is tight, cut lower-signal items like Slack/Teams since they’re ubiquitous.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Collaboration tools may feel low-value unless tied to operational impact elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email/newsletter leadership already appears in recent roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade systems over basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if Mailchimp was limited or older, consider dropping it to sharpen seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience already showing email/newsletter leadership; avoid repeating “email campaigns” elsewhere unless you add metrics or platform-specific outcomes.
- “Engagement” may also overlap with core competency “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item tool-focused, not functional.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is a bit broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and team-building contributions without repeating website/video themes already covered above.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make contributions more concrete: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten the management line: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped supervise a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this item as launching/building the capability rather than scaling it.
- “Website refresh” may feel repetitive with the later full Drupal redesign; keep this framed as an earlier refresh, not a major modernization lead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes so it complements—rather than repeats—the later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including web and program-support materials.”
- Elevate the strongest achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already cover web/video/social leadership; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since stronger management evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
